claims.claim_text: Qwen3.8-Max scored 86.6 on TerminalBench-2.1, ahead of every other model including Fable 5
Qwen3.8-Max posted a leading score of 93.0 on PaperBench, ahead of Fable 5's 88.8

Qwen3.8-Max scored 74.8 on CoWorkBench and 53.4 on JobBench, ahead of its predecessor Qwen 3.7 Max but behind Fable 5

9.summary: According to five claims from freepressjournal.in, Qwen3.8-Max scored 86.6 on TerminalBench-2.1, outperforming all other models including Fable 5, and achieved a top score of 93.0 on PaperBench, ahead of Fable 5's 88.8. On the FrontierSWE benchmark, Qwen3.8-Max scored 73.5, trailing behind Opus 4.8 and Fable 5. It also scored 74.8 on CoWorkBench and 53.4 on JobBench, surpassing its predecessor Qwen 3.7 Max but falling short of Fable 5. Additionally, Qwen3.8-Max led Fable 5 on OSWorld-Verified but scored lower than Fable 5 on MobileWorld.

15.summary: The Chinese startup Moonshot AI released an open-weight AI model called Kimi K3, which it claims has frontier-level performance, according to one source. Washington’s concerns over Chinese open-weight AI models increased after Moonshot AI launched Kimi K3 in late July, according to another source.

claims.claim_text: Chinese researchers are misusing a technique known as model distillation, which involves using outputs and data from powerful teacher models to train smaller student models.
The White House is concerned that model distillation undermines its export controls and infringes on the intellectual property rights of U.S. model makers.

SapienX Inc. co-founder Trevor Koverko stated that Chinese model distillation is best understood as transferring selected capabilities into cheaper, locally controlled systems and does not imply independence from frontier AI.

1.summary: Chinese researchers are reportedly misusing a technique called model distillation, which uses outputs and data from powerful teacher models to train smaller student models, according to siliconangle.com. The White House is concerned that this practice undermines U.S. export controls and infringes on the intellectual property rights of American model makers, as stated by siliconangle.com. Trevor Koverko, co-founder of SapienX Inc., characterized Chinese model distillation as transferring select capabilities into cheaper, locally controlled systems, but said it does not indicate independence from frontier AI, according to siliconangle.com.
